lines.text: The word crystal once meant ice.
In Greek the word krystallos first meant plain ice.
lines.say: In Greek the word KRIS-tuh-los first meant plain ice.

lines.text: Later it also named clear quartz, which is rock crystal.
Many ancient writers believed rock crystal was ice frozen for good.
The Roman writer Pliny said crystal is a kind of ice.
lines.say: The Roman writer PLIN-ee said crystal is a kind of ice.

lines.text: He wrote that it forms where winter snow freezes hardest.
He said it cannot bear heat, so it suits cold drinks.
Rock crystal is clear quartz, which is silicon dioxide.
Greek jewelers set it in bracelets and carved it into seals.
English has used the word crystal since before the 12th century.
lines.say: English has used the word crystal since before the twelfth century.

post.caption: The word crystal once meant ice. In Greek the word krystallos first meant plain ice, and later it also named clear quartz, which is rock crystal. Many ancient writers believed rock crystal was ice frozen for good. The Roman writer Pliny said crystal is a kind of ice and wrote that it forms where winter snow freezes hardest. He said it cannot bear heat, so it suits cold drinks. Rock crystal is clear quartz, which is silicon dioxide. Greek jewelers set it in bracelets and carved it into seals. English has used the word crystal since before the 12th century.
